evidence.role: meter-purpose prerequisite and later placement demand; original recall wording

hints: Recall which meter is placed in a current path.
Recall the quantity compared between two component terminals.

walkthrough.text: Match the ammeter to the Topic 9 quantity electric current.
Match the voltmeter to the Topic 9 quantity potential difference.
State both pairings: an ammeter measures electric current, and a voltmeter measures potential difference.

ai_rubric.observable: States that an ammeter measures electric current
States that a voltmeter measures potential difference

evidence.role: standard-symbol identification pattern; a different component and original options are used

hints: Compare only the fixed-resistor and variable-resistor symbols.
Look for the feature that suggests adjustment.

walkthrough.text: Begin with the fixed-resistor symbol, a plain resistor rectangle.
The variable-resistor symbol keeps the resistor and adds a diagonal arrow to show that the setting can be adjusted.
Therefore select A.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A, identifying the diagonal arrow as the distinguishing feature of a variable resistor

evidence.role: single-loop connectivity pattern; original cell-switch-lamp context

hints: Ignore where the components sit on the page.
Trace whether one unbroken path returns to its starting point.

walkthrough.text: A complete circuit needs a continuous closed path.
An unconnected terminal leaves a gap, and closeness on the page does not create a connection.
Only option C describes a path that passes through every required component and returns to the cell.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C, identifying a continuous returning path as the complete circuit

evidence.role: voltmeter-placement demand; original lamp-only multiple choice

hints: Potential difference compares two points.
Identify the two points that bound the lamp.

walkthrough.text: A voltmeter compares the potentials at its two connection points.
To measure across the lamp, those points must be the two lamp terminals.
Therefore select B.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, placing the voltmeter across the two terminals of the lamp

evidence.role: symbol identification and voltmeter-placement patterns combined in an original fault-diagnosis context

hints: Use the distinctive marks inside or around X and Y.
For the connection fault, compare the voltmeter endpoints with the endpoints of Y.

walkthrough.text: Read each labelled symbol before judging the connections.
Then trace the voltmeter path and compare its endpoints with the two terminals of Y.

hints: X has a visible break with a raised contact.
Y is a circle containing a cross.

walkthrough.text: The raised contact and gap identify X as an open switch.
The circle with a cross identifies Y as a lamp.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies X as an open switch
Identifies Y as a lamp

evidence.role: voltmeter-placement pattern in an original repair task

hints: A voltmeter needs a separate route between two selected points.
Choose the two points immediately before and after Y.

walkthrough.text: The voltmeter is incorrectly on the main path, so remove it from that series position.
Mark the two terminals of lamp Y.
Reconnect the voltmeter on its own branch from one terminal of Y to the other, so it is across Y only.

ai_rubric.observable: Removes the voltmeter from its series position in the main loop
Reconnects the voltmeter across the two terminals of lamp Y

evidence.role: series-loop construction and voltmeter placement patterns in an original greenhouse context

hints: Build the one stated path before adding anything across a component.
After the loop is complete, locate the two lamp terminals.

walkthrough.text: Translate the component list into the prescribed symbols.
Place every listed main-path component in one complete loop.
Add the voltmeter only after locating the two lamp terminals.

evidence.role: single-path circuit construction pattern with original components

hints: List the five symbols before drawing wires.
Trace one path that visits each component and returns to the battery.

walkthrough.text: Draw the prescribed battery, closed-switch, ammeter, thermistor and lamp symbols.
Join them in one continuous path with no branch and no gap.
Trace from the battery through all four other components and back to the battery to confirm the loop.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws the prescribed symbols for the battery, closed switch and ammeter
Draws the prescribed symbols for the thermistor and lamp
Connects all five components in one complete uninterrupted loop

evidence.role: voltmeter-across-component construction pattern with original component set

hints: Mark the two ends of the lamp.
The voltmeter needs one lead at each marked end.

walkthrough.text: Locate the two lamp terminals in the completed loop.
Draw a separate branch joining those same two terminals.
Place the prescribed voltmeter symbol on that branch, so the voltmeter is across the lamp only.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws the prescribed voltmeter symbol on a separate branch
Connects the two ends of the voltmeter branch to the two terminals of the lamp

evidence.role: integrated schematic construction and meter-placement demand in an original branched test-bench context

hints: Translate each connection sentence separately before combining them.
Use the Topic 9 meter purposes to check the final endpoints.

walkthrough.text: Build the complete supply path and two named component branches.
Add the voltmeter across only the LDR terminals.
Use the measured quantities to justify the ammeter and voltmeter positions.

evidence.role: whole-demand synthesis using an original topology and component set

hints: Draw the two junctions before placing the LDR and lamp.
Check that the voltmeter branch has exactly the same endpoints as the LDR.

walkthrough.text: Draw the prescribed symbols for the cell, closed switch, ammeter, LDR, lamp and voltmeter.
Connect the cell, switch and ammeter on the complete supply path leading to two junctions.
Place the LDR on one branch and the lamp on a second branch between those same two junctions.
Connect the voltmeter from one LDR terminal to the other without including the lamp in its measured span.
Trace every path and compare all branch endpoints with the written description.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the prescribed symbols for the cell, closed switch, ammeter, LDR, lamp and voltmeter
Draws a complete supply path containing the cell, closed switch and ammeter
Connects the LDR and lamp on separate branches between the same two junctions
Connects the voltmeter across the two terminals of the LDR only

evidence.role: meter-placement reasoning made explicit in original wording

hints: Name the quantity measured by each meter before discussing its connection.
Use the phrases 'in the path' and 'across two terminals'.

walkthrough.text: From Topic 9, the ammeter measures electric current.
It is therefore placed in the measured current path, before the current reaches the two component branches.
The voltmeter measures potential difference between two points.
Its leads are therefore connected across the two LDR terminals, so it measures across the LDR only.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that the ammeter measures current and is therefore placed in the measured current path
Explains that the voltmeter measures potential difference and is therefore connected across the two LDR terminals

audit.originality: All learner prompts, contexts and planned diagrams are original and do not reproduce official wording, numerical data or figures.
audit.scope: Restricted to prescribed circuit symbols and connectivity. E.m.f., potential-difference energy definitions, internal resistance, Kirchhoff's laws and resistor-network calculations are excluded.
audit.evidence: All four canonical P2 lesson evidence IDs are recorded. Canonical P1 lesson assignment is deferred, so no P1 IDs are invented.
audit.numerical_recomputation: The lesson contains no generated numerical results. Every identity, endpoint relationship and mark allocation was independently traced and reconciled.
